note: written by twin/video/floorspace.py: three layouts of the 3-D lab's equipment (design layouts, not built labs)

rows.name: conventional
rows.title: Conventional lab
notes: Zones along a 6 ft corridor; each zone's back row against its far wall, its front row against the corridor wall, a 5 ft aisle between them.

rows.name: flat
rows.title: Automated, same floor plan
notes: 4 mobile manipulators; 24 docking targets; 3 fixed arms; 12 sample racks. A docked MiR250 (580 mm wide) leaves 0.94 m of a 5 ft aisle: less than the 1.45 m one needs to drive by, so robots wait in the aisles.

rows.name: vertical
rows.title: Vertical lab
notes: North row: glovebox, atomizer, sieving cell, two Shuttles, LPBF. South row: two Instrons, three chargers, fume hood, DED, wire EDM, packaging. East end: EOS M 400-4 and Meltio cell (no MiR dock).

ssf.source: The Guardian, Tom Ireland, 2022-09-11, 'Cloud labs and remote research aren't the future of science - they're here' (reprinted by CMU: cmu.edu/ambassadors/december-2022/pdf/guardian_cloud-labs.pdf)

austin.source: Emerald Cloud Lab press release, 2023-02-28 (PR Newswire, 'Emerald Cloud Lab to relocate state-of-the-art facility from South San Francisco to Austin')

cmu.source: The Guardian, 2022-09-11 (as above): Carnegie Mellon's cloud lab, built and run with Emerald
